record.original_question: Let Omega be a smooth strictly pseudoconvex bounded domain in C^n, and let u be a plurisubharmonic solution of class C^{1,alpha}(Omega) with alpha > 1 - 2/n satisfying (dd^c u)^n = f dV, where f is smooth and bounded below by a positive constant. Determine whether u must in fact be smooth.

evidence.quote: Question 24 (Blocki-Dinew). Let u be a plurisubharmonic function in a smooth strictly pseudoconvex bounded domain Omega subset C^n. Assume u in C^{1,alpha}(Omega), alpha > 1 - 2/n and (dd^c u)^n = f dV, with f smooth and bounded away from zero f >= epsilon > 0. Is u automatically smooth ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a smooth, bounded, strictly pseudoconvex domain, and let $u : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ be a plurisubharmonic function. Assume that
\[ u \in C^{1,\alpha}(\Omega) \quad \text{for some } \alpha > 1 - \tfrac{2}{n}, \]
and that $u$ satisfies the complex Monge–Ampère equation
\[ (dd^c u)^n = f\, dV \quad \text{on } \Omega, \]
where $dV$ is Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{C}^n$, $f \in C^{\infty}(\Omega)$, and $f \ge \varepsilon > 0$ for some constant $\varepsilon$. Determine whether $u$ must necessarily belong to $C^{\infty}(\Omega)$.
artifact.status_search_result: A direct resolution of the question (smoothness of $C^{1,\alpha}$ plurisubharmonic solutions of the nondegenerate complex Monge–Ampère equation when $\alpha > 1 - 2/n$) was not located. Known related results by Błocki–Dinew give local regularity assuming a $W^{2,p}$ bound for $p > n(n-1)$, and there is work on $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimates by Dinew–Zhang and others, but none of the located sources confirm the bootstrap from this specific Hölder threshold. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A local regularity for the complex Monge-Ampère equation
status_evidence.snippet: Local regularity proven assuming W^{2,p} control for p>n(n-1), using Trudinger methods and Kołodziej's L^q estimate.
status_evidence.claim: Known regularity results require stronger a priori bounds than C^{1,alpha} with alpha>1-2/n; the specific question is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: The C^{2,alpha} estimate of complex Monge-Ampère equation
status_evidence.snippet: C^{2,alpha} estimates for the complex Monge-Ampère equation.
status_evidence.claim: Available estimates do not start from the C^{1,alpha} hypothesis with alpha>1-2/n alone.
